clue.text: Note in her writing by divine messenger

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in tells us the note sits inside the writing

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A musical note placed in a woman's handwriting, delivered by a heavenly courier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god who carried messages for Zeus on winged sandals.

clue.text: Somewhat idle-sounding flower-girl

parts.note: the Covent Garden flower seller of Shaw's Pygmalion, whose surname Doolittle sounds like doing little, i.e. being idle

explanation.surface: A lazy-seeming girl who sells flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle is the flower-girl in Shaw's Pygmalion (and My Fair Lady); her surname suggests someone who does little.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of Shaw's Cockney flower seller, whose surname hints at idleness.

clue.text: Many a mugger MO's reformed in this big world

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, i.e. many
a mugger is an Indian crocodile, shortened to croc

indicators.note: reformed means the letters of MO's are made over in a new order

explanation.surface: A city of countless street robbers, one of whose methods has changed, in this vast world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mugger' looks like a street robber, but it is the marsh crocodile of India. 'reformed' turns MOS (from MO's) into OSM.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe as a whole, as opposed to a small model of it, is the great world.

clue.text: Kind — that's Sally

parts.note: a kind or type is a sort
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is kind, that being Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a girl's name, but it is a sudden rush out by besieged troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a military dash out from a defended position.

clue.text: Court terribly slack — legal bigwig will sit on it

definitions.text: legal bigwig will sit on it

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters of slack are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A court proves dreadfully lax, and a senior judge is going to sit on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court, matching the legal theme, but it is the verb meaning to woo. The Woolsack is the wool-stuffed seat of the Lord Chancellor (now the Lord Speaker) in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chancellor, Britain's top legal officer, traditionally sat on a wool-stuffed cushion in the Lords.

clue.text: Brother Muslim, unlike the lilies of the field

definitions.meaning: a member of a Sufi Muslim religious brotherhood

definitions.text: unlike the lilies of the field
definitions.meaning: the Gospel lilies toil not, neither do they spin; these men spin round in ecstatic dance

explanation.surface: A Muslim brother who, unlike the Bible's lilies, does spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew 6:28 says the lilies of the field 'toil not, neither do they spin'; these dancers spin as worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi brother famed for spinning in ritual dance, so plainly not a lily that never spins.

clue.text: Nothing like devouring poetry when abroad

indicators.note: devouring means the first pieces swallow up the poetry, which ends up inside them

parts.note: O is the round figure nought
as means like
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Nothing compares to gobbling up poems while on holiday in foreign parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text had a stray 'devo', an OCR error; the page has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being in foreign countries across the sea.

clue.text: Form lying on the beach

definitions.meaning: a framework or outline, as in the bare structure of a building
a seashell is a thing found on the sand

explanation.surface: A shape stretched out on the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's carcass and a mollusc's casing washed up on sand share the same word.

clue.text: Main line message

parts.note: main is the sea, so a line under the main is a submarine telegraph wire carrying a telegram

explanation.surface: A message from the principal railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main line' suggests a railway; 'the main' is poetic for the ocean, crossed by undersea telegraph lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram sent by submarine cable across the ocean.

clue.text: Roving with one's tykes in a steep descent

indicators.note: in tells us these pieces go inside the descent

parts.note: a dive is a steep plunge
one is I, and the 's makes IS
tykes are mongrel dogs, curs

explanation.surface: Walking about with your mongrels down a sheer slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Discursive talk rambles from topic to topic, wandering.

clue.text: Whence Corporal Violet was able to return

indicators.note: to return means the word able is read back to front

explanation.surface: The place from which Napoleon could get back.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporal Violet was a nickname for Napoleon, who escaped from exile on this island; 'able' backwards also recalls the palindrome 'Able was I ere I saw Elba'.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon escaped from exile on this Mediterranean island in 1815.

clue.text: Black girl student has no entry in this old form of tenure

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; it describes the feudal tenure, as in its tenure

indicators.note: entry tells us the word no gets put into the pieces around it

parts.note: a Black Maria is a police van, so the girl here is Maria
taken as written
L is the learner plate, for a student driver

explanation.surface: A Black student lacks admission under an ancient system of land holding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no entry' looks like being refused admission, but NO is the thing that enters MARIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudal land holding was organised by the lord's estate, so tenure of this kind relates to a lord's estate.

clue.text: John's not short of cash

definitions.meaning: not short means long, so this is Long John, the pirate of Treasure Island

explanation.surface: John has plenty of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Long John Silver is the one-legged pirate of Stevenson's Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John's surname, and a word for coins made of the white metal.

clue.text: Fire mostly to scare birds

indicators.note: mostly means take all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: Fire a gun, more or less, to frighten off birds.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive away birds or animals with a wave and a cry.

clue.text: Pain made breath difficult before run perhaps

indicators.note: difficult signals breath is put into a laboured new order
perhaps signals the letters of run are a possible rearrangement

explanation.surface: Pain that made it hard to breathe before going for a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' turns BREATH into HEARTB; 'perhaps' turns RUN into URN.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion causing a burning ache behind the breastbone.

clue.text: Old-style cowboy there — and new-style?

indicators.note: new-style suggests the words are given a modern makeover, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned cowboy there, and a modern one?
explanation.walkthrough: Old-style is the definition (an archaic word); new-style tells you to rearrange 'there and'. A cowboy here is a cowherd.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a cowherd, neat being old English for cattle.

clue.text: Most colourful player at Twickenham ?

parts.note: a rugby man from the ... club, who play in Twickenham, and also the multicoloured pantomime character

explanation.surface: The brightest-dressed rugby player at England's home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the London home of English rugby, and also of the Harlequins rugby club; the pantomime figure wears multicoloured diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Harlequins club, whose namesake is the motley-clad comic of pantomime.

clue.text: Places where different clubs used, we hear, to supply drink

indicators.note: we hear means the golf places are said aloud, giving a same-sounding phrase

parts.note: in golf the putter is used on the green and the driver on the tee

explanation.surface: Spots where various golf clubs were wielded, it seems, to provide a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' looks like part of 'used to supply', but it belongs to the golf places.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfermented tea, popular in China and Japan, is a beverage.

clue.text: Declared a defaulter, as a lot may be?

definitions.meaning: on the London Stock Exchange a member who could not pay was formally announced with hammer strokes
an auction lot is knocked down by the auctioneer's gavel

explanation.surface: Announced as a bad debtor, as a lot might be.
explanation.walkthrough: On the old Stock Exchange a defaulting member was hammered: announced by three strokes of a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the stroke of a gavel: one ends a broker's career, the other sells a sale item.

clue.text: The end for all classical wayfarers

definitions.text: The end for all classical wayfarers

parts.words: The end for all classical wayfarers
parts.note: the saying goes that all roads lead to the ancient capital

explanation.surface: The final destination of every traveller in antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'all roads lead to' this city makes it every ancient traveller's goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian capital, which the proverb says every road leads to.

clue.text: Leading centre-half hit — out of the race

indicators.note: out signals the letters are knocked out of order
leading means the front part of the word centre is taken
half says just three of the six letters of centre are wanted

explanation.surface: A top centre-half lashes out, from the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre-half' looks like a football position, but 'Leading' and 'half' take CEN, the front half of 'centre'; 'out' then mixes CEN with HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic means relating to a people or racial group.

clue.text: Butt for actors too gets a part

indicators.note: a part says the answer is a section of the run of words

explanation.surface: A target for performers, too, is given a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt for actors' looks like the whole definition; 'Butt' alone is, and the letters run across actorS TOO GEts.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is the target of a comedian's jokes, a fall guy.

clue.text: Chest (no lid) for sale on this

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: goods on it are for sale

indicators.note: no lid means the top, i.e. first letter, is removed

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest

explanation.surface: A strongbox missing its top is up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Things 'on offer' are available to buy.

clue.text: About to get fish out of river, to economize

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: out of means the fish is placed outside the river

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: About to catch fish out of a river, in order to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' looks like landing a fish, but it means TENCH goes outside R.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to cut back spending, to save.

clue.text: Deeply romantic fissure in Xanadu's hillside

definitions.text: Deeply romantic fissure in Xanadu's hillside

parts.words: Deeply romantic fissure in Xanadu's hillside
parts.note: Coleridge's Kubla Khan speaks of the deep romantic gorge slanting down the green hill in Xanadu

explanation.surface: A deep, romantic crack in the hill at Xanadu.
explanation.walkthrough: From Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan: 'that deep romantic chasm which slanted / Down the green hill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep cleft in the earth, the one in Coleridge's poem.

clue.text: Polish enthusiast

definitions.meaning: a fan, as in a film devotee

explanation.surface: An eager fan from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital wants to be the nationality; it is the verb to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine with soft leather, and a keen fan of a subject.

clue.text: The shape, frankly, of the Cape of Good Hope

definitions.text: The shape, frankly, of the Cape of Good Hope

parts.words: The shape, frankly, of the Cape of Good Hope
parts.note: frankly refers to franking post: the Cape of Good Hope's famous early postage stamps were three-cornered

explanation.surface: To be honest, the outline of South Africa's southern cape.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cape of Good Hope colony issued famous three-cornered stamps from 1853; 'frankly' points to postage, not candour.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-sided, the outline of the Cape colony's famous stamps.

clue.text: Chancellor sadly docked two quid for trespass

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are jumbled, and docked that some are cut away

parts.note: a quid is a pound, L, so two quid gives two Ls

explanation.surface: The Chancellor regrettably had two pounds cut, for intruding.
explanation.walkthrough: Take two Ls (L = pound, from Latin libra; quid is British slang for a pound) out of CHANCELLOR and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude on another's land or rights.

clue.text: Pictures men of intelligence to include others who are backward

indicators.note: to include means the agency takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency, is staffed by intelligence men

indicators.note: who are backward says the word for others is read in reverse

parts.note: others, other people, are taken as men

explanation.surface: Clever men take in some slow-witted people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like slow-witted, but it is the reversal signal; 'Pictures' as a plural noun is British for going to the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is going to see films.
